title.en: Edinburgh Audio Tour: Monuments, Myths & Mysteries of the Old Town

events.description: A spire pierces the Edinburgh sky, blackened by centuries of secrets and storms. The city below shudders with history both whispered and shouted. Uncover a side of Edinburgh most never see on this self-guided audio tour. Move from the looming Scott Monument to the timeworn stones of Greyfriars Kirk, through the halls of New College and beyond, chasing the tales that haunt every step. Why did a silent midnight duel near the kirk change the fate of a nation? Which monument conceals the scars of a forgotten rebellion? What odd ritual once echoed through New College’s secluded courtyards? Wander ancient closes and grand crescents. Trace the city’s shadows and scandals in corners tourists rush past. Every moment here tilts between awe and revelation, promising fresh eyes on a living legend. Take the first step into Edinburgh’s tangled heart and let its true story unfold.

This year’s Cannes Palme d’Or winner stars two 2025 Oscar nominees - Renate Reinsve (Sentimental Value) and Sebastian Stan (The Apprentice) - in a gripping, morally complex drama that will leave you thinking about it long after the credits roll. A Romanian-Norwegian family moves to a small village at the end of a beautiful fjord. They quickly befriend their neighbours and their children settle into school. But when bruises are discovered on their daughter, rumours begin to spread. Is something wrong at home, or are they simply raising their children differently from everyone else? Winning his second Palme d’Or after 2007’s 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, Romanian director Cristian Mungiu turns a seemingly peaceful village into the setting for a tense, unsettling moral drama that refuses easy answers. Sebastian Stan gives an impressively restrained performance as the father, while Renate Reinsve is a calm, disquieting presence as his Norwegian wife. Slowly and surely, Fjord transforms an everyday community dispute into something far more disturbing.

events.description: We are pleased to present a major solo show by Aberdeen-based printmaker Ade Adesina (b.1980. Nigeria), bringing together an expansive collection of the artist’s monumental woodcuts, etchings, linocuts and screen-prints. Exploring urgent global themes, including climate change and colonial histories, Adesina draws from the past and present, to imagine possible futures. His works carefully balance beauty with a darker underbelly, revealing the impact of human intervention on the natural world. Informed by his African roots, combined with the influence of British culture and global travels, Adesina’s practice is steeped in the traditions of Fine Art printmaking. On first glance his work appears as classical landscapes or still lifes, however they invite and reward closer looking, as complex narratives and entangled iconography is revealed. The exhibition will contain a newly commissioned print produced specially for Edinburgh.

Joyce Moreno has written songs recorded by a host of other greats - Elis Regina, Maria Bethânia, Gal Costa, and more, racking up over 400 written pieces. Born in Rio de Janeiro, four-times Grammy nominee, singer, composer, arranger, and instrumentalist Joyce Moreno has in her portfolio over 400 recordings of songs she has authored, interpreted by the greatest names in Brazilian popular music: from Elis Regina and Gal Costa to Milton Nascimento, Sergio Mendes, and countless others. Beyond Brazil, Joyce’s work has been recorded by Annie Lennox, Wallace Roney, Omara Portuondo, Black Eyed Peas, David Sanchez, Jon Lucien, Claus Ogerman, Gerry Mulligan, Till Brönner, Flora Purim, to name a few. Joyce’s compositions have been featured in film soundtracks (e.g., The Player by Robert Altman and Legally Blonde by Robert Luketic), animations (the Japanese anime Wolf’s Rain, in partnership with composer Yoko Kanno), TV programs, and theatrical productions. In the early 1990s, her music was embraced by DJs all over the world, starting from London, and her tune 'Aldeia de Ogum' became a massive worldwide dancefloor hit, with numerous remixes. Since the beginning of her career, Joyce’s registered trademark has been the first-person feminine voice, which she pioneered; she was the first Brazilian female songwriter to express herself in this form, opening the way for countless other artists who followed. Joyce Moreno has received four nominations for the Latin Grammy (2000, 2004, 2005, 2010), and numerous awards, worldwide and in her native Brazil.

Down In Laurel Canyon: Liverpools 7-piece time machine, reawakening the golden-age harmonies of The Mamas & The Papas, CSNY, Joni Mitchell, Neil Young, The Doors, Carole King, James Taylor & more. Expect a lush, nostalgic journey of song through the heart of Laurel Canyon. Throughout the late 60s and early 70s, Laurel Canyon, hidden deep within Californias Hollywood hills, was a hub of musicianship and counterculture, and home to some of Americas most influential artists. Down In Laurel Canyon is a 7 piece band based in Liverpool, UK, featuring professional touring musicians, re-imagining the timeless catalogue of songs that came from the Canyon in a nostalgic journey back in time. From the harmonies of dynamic supergroups, The Mamas & The Papas and CSNY to the evocative ballads of James Taylor and Joni Mitchell, join the band as they take you on a trip down memory lane and re-visit the music that was born in the Laurel Canyon Hills and stood the test of time. From Neil Young to Carole King, The Byrds to The Doors, Fleetwood Mac and The Beach Boys, theres something for everyone in songs and spirit.

events.description: Big Country: 'The Seer' 40th Anniversary Tour Celebrate 40 years of a Scottish masterpiece live at Edinburgh's premier underground venue! In 1986, Dunfermline's alt-rock icons Big Country released their seminal third studio album, The Seer. Boasting towering tracks like "Look Away", "The Teacher", and the sweeping title track, the album cemented their signature widescreen, bagpipe-inflected guitar sound in rock history. To honor this milestone, Big Country - led by co-founder and longest-serving member Bruce Watson - are heading out on a massive UK anniversary run. They land at The Liquid Room in Edinburgh on Sunday, 20th December 2026 for a monumental, high-energy performance of tracks from The Seer alongside their timeless greatest hits like "In A Big Country" and "Fields Of Fire". Special Guest: Evan Peters Presents The Alarm Adding to this historic tour, the band will be joined by very special guests Evan Peters Presents The Alarm. This run honors an emotional pact made between Bruce Watson and Mike Peters following Mike's cancer diagnosis, celebrating the triumphant survival, bond, and timeless hits of both bands live on one stage.

One of Cooder’s true calling cards is how his music is able to float in air. He is not tied to the tyranny of a snare drum or any one instrument. What the man is able to do is a blend of percussion, strings, vocals, and other wonders without names into a breathing animal all its own. This really is popular music for people beyond popularity. People that live in a time of their own. Joachim Cooder grew up surrounded by music alongside his father, legendary guitarist Ry Cooder who took him on the road at an early age on the drums, playing both live and in the studio.
